subject: Mission-critical: timebox request for Helios enterprise feature
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Mission-critical: timebox request for Helios enterprise feature

Team — quick context and an ask. Helios (external contacts copied below in the procurement thread) are at legal approval, but they have one non-negotiable requirement tied to the SOW: automatic model fallback rules + a stronger audit trail for requests that include PHI flags. If we can demonstrate a short, scoped implementation (and test harness) within three weeks, they will sign the annual contract (first-year ARR ~ $1.2M) and commit to a Dedicated capacity kickoff in Q1.

Why this is time-sensitive:
- Helios procurement has blocked until we show a concrete, timeboxed plan and a minimal demo flow they can review with compliance.
- Legal and procurement want the DPA + a technical appendix describing fallback behavior for restricted tenants.

What I'm asking product/eng for today:
1) Product: a prioritized acceptance criteria list (3–5 bullets) we can show Helios by Oct 15.
2) Eng: a scoping estimate for a 2-week spike (proof-of-concept) vs. a full 3-week MVE to be production-ready.
3) Ops/Eng: confirmation we can store additional audit fields for these requests (audit_id, model_variant_used, fallback_trigger_reason) with retention controls.

Attachments: Helios_DPA_v3.pdf (procurement asked for this appended), draft SOW. Also linking a small traffic sample (helios_traffic_sample.csv) the customer provided — they say ~80% queries will be classification-style prompts with PHI flags.

If we can agree to a 2-week spike by EOD, I will commit to running an on-site demo and getting legal to unblock. This is the closest enterprise ACV we've had this quarter and worth prioritizing.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mission-critical: timebox request for Helios enterprise feature

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear ask and revenue signal. A couple of quick clarifying questions before I can prioritize this in the roadmap: 

1) Acceptance criteria — can you give concrete examples of what Helios would consider an acceptable audit entry? Do they need PII redaction proofs, or just the metadata you listed?
2) PHI handling — are they asking for additional encryption-at-rest/KMS scoping or just stronger logging and model selection controls?
3) Test coverage — do we need to run the demo against live Helios traffic (QA dataset) or is a synthetic replay acceptable for legal review?

From a product perspective, a 2-week spike can work only if we keep the scope tight: design the fallback rule engine, add the audit fields to event schema, and wire a basic UI for toggling the tenant-level policy. Anything beyond that (e.g., full retention UI, export) pushes to ~4–6 weeks.

If Sean can confirm the minimal acceptance criteria and commit to being the internal PO for the spike, I can reprioritize the next sprint to accommodate a tight spike. Karthik — can you take a quick look at whether we have obvious infra blockers for storing the extra audit metadata?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Inference Platform
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mission-critical: timebox request for Helios enterprise feature

Marissa — answers inline. Happy to be PO for this spike and to coordinate Helios for demo windows.

1) Audit entry: minimal required fields per Helios compliance team:
   - audit_id (uuid)
   - timestamp
   - tenant_id
   - request_hash (sha256)
   - model_variant_used (e.g., base, quant, fallback-v1)
   - fallback_trigger_reason (enum: policy_flag, quota_fallback, kernel_fallback)
   - redaction_status (enum: none, redacted, partial)
They explicitly said they do not need full utterance storage for the demo — metadata + a redaction proof is sufficient for legal to proceed.

2) PHI: customer asked for an appendix describing KMS integration and that the audit store will be encrypted with their tenant-managed KMS key. They will not hand over keys for the spike demo but need the architecture described.

3) Test coverage: Helios said a synthetic replay from their sanitized sample is acceptable for legal review; for production acceptance they'll request a short controlled run with obfuscated payloads.

Commitments from sales: I can get Helios to sign a one-week scoped acceptance that the metadata and demo are adequate to move to contracting. I'm escalating to Hannah for any budget tradeoffs if engineering needs additional headcount.

Sean

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mission-critical: timebox request for Helios enterprise feature

On Thu, 01 Oct 2026 at 11:05, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Audit entry: minimal required fields per Helios compliance team: audit_id (uuid), timestamp, tenant_id, request_hash (sha256), model_variant_used, fallback_trigger_reason, redaction_status
> 2) PHI: customer asked for an appendix describing KMS integration and that the audit store will be encrypted with their tenant-managed KMS key.

Thanks Sean — this is helpful. Quick technical notes and risks:

- Storage: adding the fields to our event schema is trivial (small storage delta). The bigger work is wiring tenant-scoped KMS encryption for the audit store and ensuring key rotation policies map to the customer appendix. Ops will need a runbook.
- Fallback rules: we have the routing primitives to select a quantized variant; the missing piece is a lightweight "policy-eval" layer that can be tenant-scoped and evaluate flags in real time. Building a prod-grade policy engine is larger (~4–6 weeks). For a spike, we can implement a simplified policy evaluator (in-process, config-driven) in ~2 weeks.
- Testing: I need the helios_traffic_sample.csv (sanitized) to validate distribution and ensure KV-cache behavior isn't broken by fallback switching. Can Sean circulate that?

Estimate (ballpark):
- 2-week spike (POC): 2 engineers (backend + infra) half-time + 1 engineer (platform) half-time for ops wiring — deliverables: policy-eval POC, audit fields persisted encrypted with a placeholder KMS flow, demo harness using sanitized replay.
- Full MVE (production expectation): 4–6 weeks with hardening, UI for tenant toggles, retention UI, and key-rotation compatibility testing.

If product constraints the scope to the acceptance criteria Sean outlined and we get the sample file + confirmation Helios will accept an architecture appendix (not live keys) for the spike, I can commit to the 2-week POC. Otherwise we should plan for the 4–6 week timeline.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mission-critical: timebox request for Helios enterprise feature

Thanks all — after reading the thread I am comfortable greenlighting a 2-week spike with the following conditions:

1) Scope-lock: the spike must be limited to the items Sean listed as acceptance criteria (no UI polishing, no retention UI, no export).
2) Demoable outcome: we must produce a short replay demo using the sanitized CSV and a one-page architecture appendix that shows KMS integration and audit encryption assumptions.
3) Decision deadline: post-spike review and go/no-go will be scheduled for Oct 15. Product and Eng must present a risks list and a resource request if Helios requires production rollout beyond the initial scope.

Marissa — please create a one-page acceptance criteria doc and attach to the HubSpot deal. Karthik — please confirm the engineer allocation (names) by EOD so we can reassign sprint capacity. Sean — continue procurement engagement and push for the acceptance sign-off clause with Helios legal.

I'll authorize the spike budget from the product discretionary pool (no headcount yet). If this converts, we'll fast-track the next planning cycle for production work.

Hannah Schmitt
VP Product, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
